questions.q: What is the essay's central argument?
options: Cities send messages that strongly shape the ambitions of the people living in them
Silicon Valley will soon replace New York as the world's capital
The Internet will make physical location irrelevant to ambition
Universities are the main reason cities become great
questions.explain: The author argues each city sends a message about what to strive for, and that this force is hard to resist.

questions.q: What message does the author say Silicon Valley sends?
questions.explain: The Valley's message is 'you should be more powerful', i.e. how much effect you have on the world.

questions.q: What message did the author find Berkeley sends after living there?
options: You should do things with style
questions.explain: Berkeley is pleasant and civilized, and its message is 'you should live better'.

questions.q: In the Forbes 400, the ratio of New York to California residents moved from 1.45 in 1982 to what in 2007?
Why does the author think New York is unlikely to become a startup hub rivaling Silicon Valley?
options: Startup founders there would feel like second class citizens next to what New Yorkers admire more
New York lacks the venture capital firms needed to fund the early stage of startups
Engineers in New York are lured by banks into finance jobs that pay far more than startups
New York's universities rarely license research to startups, unlike those in the Bay Area
questions.explain: Because New York already admires something else more (money), a startup founder there would feel second class.
